name: Haus der Stille
tradition: Non-sectarian Buddhist meditation center hosting a rotating faculty of monastics and lay teachers from Theravada/Vipassana, Zen, and Tibetan Vajrayana lineages
technique: Silent sitting and walking meditation, primarily Vipassana (Insight), alongside Zen, Metta, and movement-based approaches such as qigong, Tai Chi, or yoga depending on the visiting teacher
influences: Theravada Thai Forest monastics (Bhante Sujiva, Bhante Sukhacitto, Yogavacara Rahula)
teacherAccess: A single visiting teacher (occasionally with an assistant) leads each seminar's daily group sittings and dharma talks; the degree of individual guidance or interviews depends on that teacher's own format
retreatOptions: Seminars run roughly 3 to 9 nights almost year-round (closed January-February), mostly held in noble silence; program spans Vipassana, Zen, Metta, qigong/Tai Chi and yoga-based retreats, plus an occasional family retreat and a self-organized (self-guided) silent retreat weekend
about: Haus der Stille is a Buddhist meditation center in the village of Roseburg, about 50 kilometers east of Hamburg amid quiet lakes and old deciduous woodland in Schleswig-Holstein. Founded in 1960 by the non-profit association Haus der Stille e.V., it is one of the oldest Buddhist meditation centers in Germany, based in a well-preserved 1903 manor house alongside a guest house and a dedicated meditation hall. The center is non-sectarian and open to all schools of Buddhism, hosting a rotating roster of monks, nuns, Zen teachers, lamas, and lay meditation teachers who each lead their own seminar, most often built around Vipassana practice but also Zen, Metta, and movement-based approaches like qigong or yoga. Seminars typically run three to nine nights, are held mostly in silence, and combine group sitting and walking meditation with dharma talks and a daily one-hour work period. No prior familiarity with Buddhist ideas or principles is required to attend.
schedule: Typical day runs from around 6:00 morning meditation to a 19:30 evening session, with additional sits at 9:00 and 14:30 framed by meals at 8:00, 12:00, and 18:00, plus a daily 8:30-9:30 work period; each seminar begins with dinner on the arrival afternoon (from 15:00) and ends after lunch on the departure day
cost: Pensionspreis (room and full board) is billed per night: EUR 65 for association members, EUR 70 for non-members, plus a single-room surcharge of EUR 14/night or double-room surcharge of EUR 7/night per person; on top of this, most seminars ask for voluntary dana to the visiting teacher, though some instead charge a fixed teacher fee (Lehrerhonorar); reduced rates are available on request for participants with low income

pricePerDay.notes: Standard per-night Pensionspreis (shared-room accommodation plus full board, VAT included): EUR 65 for members, EUR 70 for non-members; cross-checked against the 7-night Seminar 17/2026 (25 Jul-1 Aug 2026), where the quoted Pensionspreis was EUR 490 for non-members (= EUR 70/night) and EUR 455 for members (= EUR 65/night). Excludes the separate teacher dana/Lehrerhonorar and single (+EUR 14/night) or double (+EUR 7/night/person) room surcharges.

foodNotes: Vollpension (full board): three freshly prepared vegetarian meals a day plus water, tea, coffee, juice, and fresh fruit; the kitchen aims to use regional and organic ingredients, and dietary needs, allergies, or intolerances can be accommodated with advance notice.
workNotes: On multi-day seminars, all participants are asked to join a daily one-hour work period (kitchen, garden, or house cleaning), signed up for on arrival, following the center's long-standing tradition of keeping costs down through shared labor.
